title: Stagflation calls for flexibility in fixed income, not abandonment
summary: The article argues that stagflation, characterized by rising inflation and slowing economic growth, necessitates a flexible approach to fixed income rather than abandonment. It highlights that stagflation rarely affects all markets equally, creating regional opportunities and risks. Historically, inflation shocks are often followed by more supportive environments for fixed income returns, emphasizing the value of dynamic bond strategies that can adjust duration and invest broadly across various sectors.
